15384.title: Cross Product
15384.heading: Cross Product
15384.content:
The cross product $u\times v$ is a vector perpendicular to the plane spanned by three-dimensional vectors $u$ and $v$, with direction set by the right-hand rule. Its magnitude is $\|u\|\|v\|\sin\theta$, equal to the area of their parallelogram. It vanishes for parallel vectors.

Game code uses the cross product to construct perpendicular basis directions and surface normals. Operand order matters because reversing the vectors reverses the direction of the result.

15387.title: Cross Multiplication
15387.heading: Cross Multiplication
15387.content:
Cross multiplication solves a proportion by multiplying both sides by both nonzero denominators. From

$$\frac{a}{b}=\frac{c}{d},\qquad b,d\neq0,$$

it follows that

$$ad=bc.$$

The step is a shorthand for [[Clearing Denominators]], not a separate rule that applies to arbitrary sums of fractions. When a denominator contains a variable, values that make it zero must be excluded before the products are formed. Any resulting candidate should be verified in the original proportion.

15390.title: CRISP-DM
15390.heading: CRISP-DM
15390.content:
CRISP-DM is a cross-industry process model organized into business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, and deployment. Each phase contains practical tasks such as defining goals, checking quality, constructing attributes, designing tests, and planning monitoring.

Its business and technical phases connect modeling choices to an operational purpose. Evaluation can redirect the work to an earlier phase rather than serving only as final approval.

Kelleher and Tierney present the six phases as an iterative, vendor-independent route from a practical question to deployment. Business and data understanding inform each other: examining available records may force a better definition of the goal, while the goal determines which records and attributes are worth preparing. Evaluation asks whether the result meets the business objective as well as whether a model fits data; deployment includes using and monitoring the result, not just saving a fitted model.

15396.title: Crisp Partition
15396.heading: Crisp Partition
15396.content:
A crisp partition divides a data set into nonempty, mutually disjoint clusters whose union contains every observation. Each observation has membership one in exactly one cluster and zero in the others.

This representation is simple and decisive, but it can handle ambiguous or overlapping groups poorly. Fuzzy clustering generalizes it by permitting intermediate membership values.

15399.title: Crisp Clustering
15399.heading: Crisp Clustering
15399.content:
Crisp clustering assigns every observation to exactly one cluster. The clusters are nonempty, their union covers the data set, and distinct clusters do not overlap.

This exclusivity makes a crisp partition easy to store and interpret, but it can misrepresent gradual boundaries. [[Fuzzy Partition]] models replace the zero-or-one assignment with degrees of membership when observations plausibly belong to more than one group.

15435.title: Cox's Theorem
15435.heading: Cox's Theorem
15435.content:
Cox's theorem derives the probability rules from requirements for consistent reasoning about plausibility. Plausibility is represented numerically, equivalent ways of calculating the same claim must agree, and changes in support for a proposition must relate consistently to its negation and conjunctions.

Under these requirements, plausible reasoning follows normalization and the conjunction rule. A calculus that violates those rules contradicts at least one of the stated consistency requirements.

15438.content:
The Cox proportional hazards model relates predictors to an event hazard without specifying the baseline hazard's parametric shape. It is semiparametric: coefficients determine multiplicative hazard ratios while the baseline remains unspecified.

This flexibility avoids choosing a full event-time distribution, but the predictor effects are assumed to remain proportional over time. The [[Proportional Hazards Assumption]] must therefore be examined before the hazard ratios are accepted.

15441.content:
Fluid pressure and velocity satisfy mass and momentum conservation, while temperature satisfies energy conservation. In a nonisothermal model, advection carries thermal energy and temperature-dependent properties feed back into the momentum equations.

Boundary conditions must be compatible across all three fields: an inlet may specify flow and temperature, an outlet may constrain pressure, and walls impose both velocity and thermal behavior. Solver convergence then reflects the combined system rather than any single equation alone.

15444.heading: Countable Set
15444.content:
A set is countable when it is finite or can be put into one-to-one correspondence with the natural numbers. A countably infinite set can therefore be arranged as a sequence in which every member eventually appears.

The rational numbers are countable even though they are dense on the number line, because their integer numerator-denominator pairs can be systematically enumerated while repetitions are skipped.

$$F=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{|q_1q_2|}{r^2}.$$

The force acts along the line joining the charges and is attractive for unlike signs and repulsive for like signs. Multiple forces combine vectorially through superposition.

Cosmos DB global distribution replicates data into selected geographic regions. Placing a copy nearer to a distant user population can reduce network latency, while geographic separation can also protect availability when one location fails.

Replication has a monetary and consistency cost, so regions should reflect actual access and resilience needs. The book treats location as a physical design choice because information still takes time to travel even when the database is managed.

15468.title: Correspondence Analysis
15468.heading: Correspondence Analysis
15468.content:
Correspondence analysis maps a table of non-negative occurrences or frequencies into a factor space where relationships among rows and columns can be viewed geometrically. Rows may be scenes or documents, while columns may be words or attributes. Their profiles are compared using a chi-squared weighted distance before the factor mapping.

The method does not begin by imposing predefined classes. It uses row and column masses, principal axes of inertia, and the dual relation between observations and attributes to reveal how a record is positioned relative to the overall pattern. The book uses this platform to map semantic context and then adds hierarchical clustering to examine change.

15477.sourceSearchName: correlation based feature selection correlation based feature selection
15477.title: Correlation-Based Feature Selection
15477.heading: Correlation-Based Feature Selection
15477.content:
Correlation-based feature selection scores candidate inputs by how strongly they relate to the target or model performance. Pearson correlation can measure linear association, while ablation can reveal the loss caused by dropping one feature.

A strong correlation identifies predictive association rather than a causal mechanism. Features should also be checked for overlap because combinations of user and social signals may outperform either family alone.

More generally, correlation-based selection examines statistical dependencies among variables and with a target. It can identify irrelevant and redundant dimensions efficiently, but pairwise association may miss conditional or nonlinear usefulness.

15480.title: Correlation Plot
15480.heading: Correlation Plot
15480.content:
A correlation plot visually encodes the pairwise coefficients in a [[Correlation Matrix]]. Color, size, or shape communicates the direction and magnitude of each relationship, and clustering can reorder variables with similar patterns.

The display helps find groups of related variables and potential redundancy, but it does not establish causation. Labels, significance information, and the treatment of missing observations must remain consistent with the matrix from which the plot was produced.

15483.title: Correlation Matrix
15483.heading: Correlation Matrix
15483.content:
A correlation matrix arranges pairwise correlation coefficients for several variables in a symmetric table. The diagonal contains perfect self-correlations, while the off-diagonal cells summarize the strength and direction of each pairwise linear or rank relationship.

Missing-data rules and the chosen correlation method affect every entry. A matrix can identify redundancy or possible [[Regression Collinearity]], but it cannot determine causation or replace examination of the underlying scatter plots.

15486.content:
A correlation subspace is a set of directions along which a group follows a strong linear relationship rather than merely occupying a small axis-aligned box. Points may vary widely on individual attributes while remaining close to a lower-dimensional manifold.

Correlation clustering measures deviation from that manifold and groups points sharing a relationship. It must distinguish genuine local correlation from chance alignments and from one global trend spanning the dataset.

15489.title: Corpus Linguistics
15489.heading: Corpus Linguistics
15489.content:
Corpus linguistics is the computer-mediated study of language structure and use in collections of naturally occurring text. It searches for patterns, associations, historical changes, meanings, and sentiment while retaining attention to the contexts in which forms appear.

The method combines quantitative rigor with qualitative investigation. Rather than assuming a word has one stable meaning, it asks how the word behaves across genres, periods, and neighboring language.

15495.title: Core Resource
15495.heading: Core Resource
15495.content:
A core resource is a resource the player most depends on, seeks to maximize, or must avoid losing to continue play. It is closely tied to the game's central goals and [[Core Gameplay Loop]].

Identifying a core resource gives balancing work a common basis for comparing costs and benefits. Subsidiary resources support or modify it, while a hidden aggregate may sometimes serve as a shadow resource when several visible values contribute to one outcome.

15497.sourceSearchName: core gameplay loop core gameplay loop
15497.title: Core Gameplay Loop
15497.heading: Document

15498.sourceSearchName: core gameplay loop core gameplay loop
15498.title: Core Gameplay Loop
15498.heading: Core Gameplay Loop
15498.content:
A core gameplay loop is the interactive cycle central to the player's attention: intention leads to action, the game state changes, feedback communicates the result, and progress or reward informs the next intention.

Core does not necessarily mean fastest or innermost. A game may shift among several core loops and nest rapid loops inside slower outer loops, connecting moment-to-moment play with [[Player Goal|goals]], learning, and [[Progression System|progression]].

15501.content:
A core game prototype integrates the full set of primary player actions with goals, important rules, and win or loss conditions. It goes beyond a rough playable prototype so the central experience can be evaluated as a connected system.

Basic art and sound can be included when they materially affect understanding or feeling. Secondary content and final polish remain unnecessary unless the test question depends on them.

15504.title: Core Mechanics
15504.heading: Core Mechanics
15504.content:
Core mechanics are the algorithms and data that implement rules operating throughout a game. They maintain state, accept actions, produce consequences, present active challenges, detect success or failure, control mode changes, and support artificial opponents and story events.

The source groups major mechanical work into physics, internal economies, progression, tactical maneuvering, and social interaction. Level-specific scripts or behavior unique to one temporary character are not necessarily core mechanics.

15506.title: Copy-Move Image Forgery

15507.sourceSearchName: copy move image forgery copy move image forgery
15507.title: Copy-Move Image Forgery
15507.heading: Copy-Move Image Forgery
15507.content:
A copy-move image forgery duplicates pixels from one part of a photograph and pastes them elsewhere in the same image. It is commonly used to conceal an object, repeat a feature, or fill an area with texture that already matches the source's color, noise, and compression.

The pasted region may be translated, scaled, rotated, blended, or otherwise adjusted. Detection therefore searches for related local structure rather than exact full-image duplication, then verifies whether the matched pixels follow a coherent geometric transformation.

15508.title: Copy-Move Image Forgery

15510.title: Copy Avoidance
15510.heading: Copy Avoidance
15510.content:
Copy avoidance designs an I/O path so data does not repeatedly move between application, protocol, and device buffers. Each eliminated copy saves memory bandwidth and CPU time and can reduce latency.

The technique often requires careful buffer ownership, lifetime management, alignment, and protection because shared or directly registered memory crosses subsystem boundaries.

15513.title: Coprime Polynomials
15513.heading: Coprime Polynomials
15513.content:
Polynomials are coprime when they have no common nonconstant factor. Over a [[Field]], this is equivalent to the ideal they generate being the entire [[Polynomial Ring]].

The [[Bezout Identity for Polynomials]] then expresses 1 as a polynomial combination of the inputs. A zero [[Polynomial Resultant]] detects the opposite situation for two positive-degree polynomials: the presence of a common factor.

15515.title: Coprime Ideals
15515.heading: Document
15515.content:
2026-09-13 19:40

Status: #baby

Tags: [[Prime Ideals and Noetherian Algebra]]

15516.title: Coprime Ideals
15516.heading: Coprime Ideals
15516.content:
Two ideals I and J are coprime when I + J is the whole ring. Equivalently, there are elements a ∈ I and b ∈ J with a + b = 1.

For coprime ideals, intersection and product agree: I ∩ J = IJ. Pairwise coprimality is also the condition that makes the canonical map to a product of quotient rings surjective, a ring-level form of the Chinese remainder principle.

15518.sourceSearchName: coplanar face reduction coplanar face reduction
15518.title: Coplanar Face Reduction
15518.heading: Document

15519.sourceSearchName: coplanar face reduction coplanar face reduction
15519.title: Coplanar Face Reduction
15519.heading: Coplanar Face Reduction
15519.content:
Several adjacent triangles that lie on the same plane can sometimes be represented as one polygonal face whose boundary lists all required points. This reduces the number of face records and indices without changing the visible planar surface.

The optimization depends on the target representation supporting polygon faces. OBJ and PLY can express more than three vertices in a face, whereas STL requires triangular facets. Reduction is therefore both a geometric question about coplanarity and a format question about what the receiving system accepts.

15520.title: Coplanar Face Reduction
15520.heading: References

15522.title: Cophenetic Proximity
15522.heading: Cophenetic Proximity
15522.content:
Cophenetic proximity between two observations is the dendrogram level at which they first become members of the same cluster. Collecting these values produces a cophenetic proximity matrix.

Comparing that matrix with the original proximities measures how faithfully the hierarchy preserves pairwise relationships. The [[Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient]] is one such comparison.

15524.sourceSearchName: cophenetic correlation coefficient cophenetic correlation coefficient
15524.title: Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient
15524.heading: Document

15525.sourceSearchName: cophenetic correlation coefficient cophenetic correlation coefficient
15525.title: Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient
15525.heading: Cophenetic Correlation Coefficient
15525.content:
The cophenetic correlation coefficient is the product-moment correlation between original pairwise proximities and the cophenetic proximities encoded by a dendrogram. A value near one indicates that the hierarchy preserves the pairwise structure well.

Only one triangle of symmetric proximity matrices is needed for the calculation. A high coefficient measures faithful distance representation, not necessarily domain correctness.

15531.title: Coordinated Checkpointing
15531.heading: Coordinated Checkpointing
15531.content:
Coordinated checkpointing records a consistent recovery state across the processes of a parallel application. After a failure, the application can resume from that saved state rather than restart from the beginning.

Frequent checkpoints reduce lost computation but add more storage and synchronization overhead. The useful interval depends on failure rate and checkpoint cost.

15534.title: Coordinate Rotation
15534.heading: Coordinate Rotation
15534.content:
A coordinate rotation expresses the same points relative to a new orthonormal basis. The coordinates change, but an orthogonal rotation preserves Euclidean distances and total sum of squares.

The source uses rotation to align a new axis with the direction of strongest shared variation in paired measurements. Once aligned, a small number of rotated coordinates can approximate the data more effectively than the original axes.

15537.title: Coordinate Reference System
15537.heading: Coordinate Reference System
15537.content: A coordinate reference system defines how numeric coordinates correspond to locations on the Earth. It includes a datum and may include a projection that transforms the curved surface into planar coordinates. Spatial layers must use compatible systems before their geometries can be overlaid correctly. [[Spatial Data Reprojection]] changes coordinate values between systems; merely relabeling coordinates does not perform that transformation.

15540.title: Cooperative Play Structures
15540.heading: Cooperative Play Structures
15540.content:
Cooperative play asks participants to coordinate toward a shared outcome. Symmetrical cooperation gives players similar capabilities, asymmetrical cooperation divides capabilities by role, and symbiotic cooperation makes each participant depend on contributions others cannot supply.

A shared goal alone does not guarantee cooperation. The design must create interdependence, information exchange, or complementary action so that collaboration changes what the group can achieve.

15542.sourceSearchName: conway s law conway s law
15542.title: Conway's Law

Tags: [[Scaling Agile Teams]] [[Bounded Context and Organizational Design]]

15543.sourceSearchName: conway s law conway s law
15543.title: Conway's Law
15543.heading: Conway's Law
15543.content:
Conway's Law observes that a system's design tends to reproduce the communication structure of the organization that creates it. Teams separated by technology, discipline, or feature area often produce corresponding seams in the product.

Organizational design is therefore also product design. Cross-discipline feature teams and shared whole-game goals can reduce fragmentation that a component-centered hierarchy would otherwise embed.

In a domain-centered organization, teams divided by technical layer tend to produce matching seams and coordination queues. Cross-functional teams aligned to business capabilities can instead own one or more [[Bounded Context]]s. A context should not be split across multiple owners when that would require continuous agreement about its internal model.

15544.sourceSearchName: conway s law conway s law
15544.title: Conway's Law
15544.heading: References

15546.title: Cooperation
15546.heading: Cooperation
15546.content:
Cooperation is a form of play in which participants act together toward shared goals. Their actions can be complementary, coordinated, or mutually supportive rather than directed against one another.

A cooperative game still needs challenges and meaningful decisions. The design must make joint action matter so that one participant does not perform all important work while the others merely observe.

15548.sourceSearchName: convolutional weight sharing convolutional weight sharing
15548.title: Convolutional Weight Sharing
15548.heading: Document

15549.sourceSearchName: convolutional weight sharing convolutional weight sharing
15549.title: Convolutional Weight Sharing
15549.heading: Convolutional Weight Sharing
15549.content:
Convolutional weight sharing means that neurons inspecting different image locations use the same learned weights. Because the weights define a detector, those neurons search for the same pattern in different [[CNN Receptive Field|receptive fields]]. A feature can be found wherever a member of the shared group responds, rather than requiring a separately learned detector at each position.

Sharing also reduces the number of trainable parameters compared with assigning independent weights to every local neuron. It supplies a useful spatial assumption to a [[Convolutional Neural Network]]: the local pattern worth detecting may recur at multiple locations. Pooling can add tolerance to location, but it can also discard information about the arrangement of parts.

15550.sourceSearchName: convolutional weight sharing convolutional weight sharing
15550.title: Convolutional Weight Sharing
15550.heading: References

15552.title: Convolutional Stride
15552.heading: Convolutional Stride
15552.content:
Stride length is the distance a convolutional detector moves between successive locations on an input. In the book's image example, a stride of one moves each [[CNN Receptive Field|receptive field]] one position from its neighbor, so the fields overlap substantially. Increasing stride reduces that overlap.

Stride is a [[Hyperparameter]] chosen before training rather than a kernel weight learned from data. It affects which local regions are inspected and how densely their responses appear in the [[Convolutional Feature Map]]. A larger step can make the map coarser, so the stride should match the scale of the patterns the architecture needs to preserve.

15554.sourceSearchName: convolutional neural network convolutional neural network
15554.title: Convolutional Neural Network
15554.heading: Document

15555.sourceSearchName: convolutional neural network convolutional neural network
15555.title: Convolutional Neural Network
15555.heading: Convolutional Neural Network
15555.content:
A convolutional neural network applies learned filters across local regions of an input. Shared filter weights allow the same pattern to be detected at different positions while using fewer parameters than dense connections.

Although strongly associated with images, convolution can also find local structure in speech representations. It can complement sequence models by detecting short acoustic patterns in a [[Feature Vector|feature sequence]].

Kelleher explains the image architecture through [[CNN Receptive Field|local receptive fields]], [[Convolutional Weight Sharing|shared weights]], and a learned [[Convolutional Kernel|kernel]] that produces a [[Convolutional Feature Map|feature map]] across positions. An activation function transforms the map, and a [[CNN Pooling Layer|pooling layer]] may downsample it. A [[CNN Filter Bank|bank of filters]] detects multiple patterns; later [[CNN Dense Layer Integration|dense layers]] can combine those responses for a whole-object decision. [[Residual Skip Connection|Skip connections]] are one extension used to train very deep versions of this architecture.

15556.sourceSearchName: convolutional neural network convolutional neural network
15556.title: Convolutional Neural Network
15556.heading: References

15558.title: Convolutional Kernel
15558.heading: Convolutional Kernel
15558.content:
A convolutional kernel is a small learned matrix of weights applied to a local image patch. At each [[CNN Receptive Field|receptive field]], the inputs are weighted and summed with the same kernel. Moving this calculation across the image records where its associated local pattern occurs.

The kernel itself performs the weighted-sum part of processing, not the nonlinear activation. A [[Convolutional Feature Map]] records its position-by-position outputs; a later activation function can then transform those values. Multiple kernels let a [[Convolutional Neural Network]] look for different features in parallel.

15560.sourceSearchName: convolutional feature transfer convolutional feature transfer
15560.title: Convolutional Feature Transfer
15560.heading: Document

15561.sourceSearchName: convolutional feature transfer convolutional feature transfer
15561.title: Convolutional Feature Transfer
15561.heading: Convolutional Feature Transfer
15561.content:
Convolutional feature transfer reuses internal activations from a neural network trained on one image task as features for another. Earlier layers often capture broadly useful edges and textures, while later layers are more specialized.

A target task may freeze the pretrained network, extract fixed feature maps, or fine-tune selected layers. Transfer is strongest when the source and target visual domains share relevant structure.

15562.sourceSearchName: convolutional feature transfer convolutional feature transfer
15562.title: Convolutional Feature Transfer
15562.heading: References

15563.sourceSearchName: convolutional feature map convolutional feature map
15563.title: Convolutional Feature Map
15563.heading: Document

15564.sourceSearchName: convolutional feature map convolutional feature map
15564.title: Convolutional Feature Map
15564.heading: Convolutional Feature Map
15564.content:
A feature map records the output of one [[Convolutional Kernel]] at each location where the kernel is applied. It is a spatial account of how strongly the learned local detector responded across an image, not merely a single yes-or-no answer for the whole image.

A nonlinear [[Activation Function]] is commonly applied element by element to the map before a [[CNN Pooling Layer]] downsamples it. Maps from different kernels can also be combined and passed to a later convolutional layer. This lets the network build features from earlier detections while preserving spatial information until the architecture chooses to reduce it.

15565.sourceSearchName: convolutional feature map convolutional feature map
15565.title: Convolutional Feature Map
15565.heading: References

15567.title: Convex Function
15567.heading: Convex Function
15567.content:
A function is convex on a [[Convex Set]] when every chord between two points on its graph lies on or above the graph. Equivalently, for $0\leq t\leq1$, $f(tx+(1-t)y)\leq tf(x)+(1-t)f(y)$.

For a differentiable convex function, local minima are global minima. A twice-differentiable function is convex where its [[Hessian Matrix]] is positive semidefinite.

15570.title: Convex Set
15570.heading: Convex Set
15570.content:
A set is convex when the line segment joining any two of its points remains entirely inside the set. For points $x$ and $y$, every combination $tx+(1-t)y$ with $0\leq t\leq1$ must remain in the set.

Convex feasible regions prevent separated pockets of admissible solutions. A [[Convex Function]] defined on a convex set has especially useful global optimization properties.

15573.heading: Conversion-Factor Chains
15573.content: When no convenient direct factor is used, several compatible ratios can be multiplied in sequence. The book converts nautical miles to fathoms through kilometers and meters: $\mathrm{nmi}\times\mathrm{km/nmi}\times\mathrm{m/km}\times\mathrm{ftm/m}$ leaves only fathoms. The intermediate units cancel regardless of the values carried by their factors. Writing the units alongside each ratio exposes a reversed factor or missing step before a calculator result is accepted. See [[Unit Conversion Factor]] and [[Dimensional Homogeneity in Equations]].

15576.title: Converter
15576.heading: Converter
15576.content:
A converter transforms one kind of [[Resource]] into another resource or object. The input is consumed by the conversion while the output is created.

Converters may have one input and output or form long production chains with multiple requirements and by-products. Additional conversion detail is valuable only when it produces meaningful decisions rather than needless [[Cognitive Load]].

15579.sourceSearchName: conversion resolution versus accuracy conversion resolution versus accuracy
15579.title: Conversion Resolution versus Accuracy
15579.heading: Conversion Resolution versus Accuracy
15579.content: Resolution is the number of digits presented in a measurement or calculation; accuracy concerns how well those digits represent the intended quantity. The book warns that a conversion result with many displayed places can appear more trustworthy than the starting observation warrants. It gives 1000 as an ambiguous example: the app initially reads four significant digits, but an estimate to the nearest thousand should be reported with only one. The user must supply that context because the digits alone cannot settle it. See [[Significant Digits in Unit Conversion]].

15580.sourceSearchName: conversion resolution versus accuracy conversion resolution versus accuracy

15581.sourceSearchName: conversational reference resolution conversational reference resolution
15581.title: Conversational Reference Resolution
15581.heading: Document

15582.sourceSearchName: conversational reference resolution conversational reference resolution
15582.title: Conversational Reference Resolution
15582.heading: Conversational Reference Resolution
15582.content:
Conversational reference resolution identifies what a referring expression points to in the current interaction. Pronouns and phrases such as “that one” or “there” often depend on entities introduced in earlier turns or shown on a display.

Resolution uses [[Conversation Context]] and sometimes multimodal state. When several referents remain plausible, the [[Dialog Manager]] should use a [[Clarification Question]] rather than silently choose a risky action.

15583.sourceSearchName: conversational reference resolution conversational reference resolution
15583.title: Conversational Reference Resolution
15583.heading: References

15585.title: Conversational Ability
15585.heading: Conversational Ability
15585.content:
Conversational ability is a system's capacity to exchange turns in natural language while preserving enough meaning and context to move an interaction forward. It depends on more than recognizing words: the system must interpret intent, manage state, choose actions, and express responses.

Conversational fluency is not a reliable measure of general intelligence. A system can produce socially plausible language while having little knowledge or utility beyond a narrow [[Intent Schema]].

15588.title: Conversation Context
15588.heading: Conversation Context
15588.content:
Conversation context is the information carried across turns that affects how a new utterance should be interpreted. It includes prior intents, mentioned entities, questions asked, values supplied, and unresolved goals.

The [[Dialog Manager]] uses this state for [[Conversational Reference Resolution]], interpreting [[Elliptical Utterance|elliptical utterances]], and avoiding repeated questions. Context turns isolated sentences into a coherent interaction.

15591.heading: Converged Networked Storage
15591.content:
Converged networked storage carries remote storage traffic over the same general network technology used for ordinary communication, commonly Ethernet. Consolidation can simplify cabling and management while using widely available hardware.

The shared fabric must still meet storage expectations for latency, throughput, loss handling, ordering, and isolation from unrelated network traffic.

15594.title: Convention over Configuration
15594.heading: Convention over Configuration
15594.content:
Convention over configuration lets a framework infer ordinary behavior from established names and structures, requiring explicit settings only when a model differs from those defaults. This reduces repetitive setup while preserving an escape path for exceptional cases.

[[Entity Framework Core]] uses conventions to recognize entity keys and relationships. [[Data Annotation|annotations]] or model-building code can then override or extend those inferred mappings.

15597.title: Convenience-Privacy Tradeoff
15597.heading: Convenience-Privacy Tradeoff
15597.content:
The convenience-privacy tradeoff occurs when a mobile service reduces effort or provides faster information in exchange for access to personal data. Location-aware results and personalized services can make disclosure feel immediately worthwhile.

The tradeoff is difficult to evaluate because convenience is present and visible while privacy costs may be delayed, uncertain, or distributed across future uses. This asymmetry contributes to the [[Consumer Privacy Paradox]].

15600.heading: Controller Action Method
15600.content:
A controller action method handles a routed HTTP operation. Its parameters receive bound request data, its body coordinates application work, and its return value communicates a response body and status to the client.

Action methods can be asynchronous when repository operations wait on external resources. Their signatures also document which request values are required and which response shapes callers can expect.

15603.sourceSearchName: convective heat transfer coefficient convective heat transfer coefficient
15603.title: Convective Heat Transfer Coefficient
15603.heading: Convective Heat Transfer Coefficient
15603.content:
Newton's law of cooling expresses convective heat rate as $q=Ah(T_s-T_\infty)$. The coefficient $h$ packages the effect of fluid velocity, orientation, surface condition, and other flow characteristics on exchange between a wall and the surrounding bulk fluid.

Because $h$ represents a coupled transport process, it is not generally a fixed material property. Correlations or experiments supply an effective value, and [[Thermal Model Verification and Sensitivity|sensitivity analysis]] should test its influence when flow conditions are uncertain.

15606.title: Controlled Component
15606.heading: Controlled Component
15606.content:
A controlled component is a form element whose displayed value is synchronized with React state. The component supplies the current value and handles change events by updating that state.

This makes the React model the source of truth for the field, allowing validation and submission to read consistent values. A form with many controlled fields can produce repetitive handlers, motivating a [[Generic Form Component]].

15609.title: Control Structure
15609.heading: Control Structure
15609.content:
A control structure determines how the steps of an [[Algorithm]] or program are combined and which step executes next. Three forms are sufficient to organize algorithmic procedures: [[Sequence Control Structure|sequence]], [[Selection Control Structure|selection]], and [[Iteration Control Structure|iteration]].

Sequence places steps one after another. Selection chooses between alternatives according to a condition. Iteration repeats steps until a stopping condition is satisfied. Complex algorithms arise from nesting and composing these basic structures rather than requiring fundamentally different forms of control.

15612.title: Control Storage Calculation and Communication
15612.heading: Control Storage Calculation and Communication
15612.content:
Control, storage, calculation, and communication are four historical streams that converged in digital computing. Control selects operations, storage preserves encoded state, calculation transforms it, and communication moves it across distance.

A programmable networked computer coordinates all four. The convergence explains why computing grew beyond arithmetic into a general infrastructure for information.

15615.title: Control Creep
15615.heading: Control Creep
15615.content:
Control creep is the repurposing of data or monitoring infrastructure from its initial function into a wider system of regulation or surveillance. A camera or sensor installed to manage traffic may later become a source for security investigations.

The new use can be defended as beneficial, but it changes the relationship between the system and the people recorded by it. The book argues that joining sources and repeatedly expanding purposes can make ordinary actions appear suspicious in an anticipatory governance system. Purpose and limits need renewed scrutiny whenever a dataset changes roles.
